issues: The sentence “Mamba matched its strong Transformer++ recipe, especially as sequence length grew, and outperformed the listed attention-free models” does not retain the paper’s important comparison qualification: full 8K results were missing for RWKV and RetNet because the available implementations ran out of memory or required unrealistic computation. “Listed” is too vague to prevent readers from assuming every named attention-free baseline was compared throughout the longer-context result. Add that caveat while preserving that the reported comparisons favor Mamba in the reported 125M–1.3B Pile scaling experiments.

In “the implementation loads the needed SSM parameters into faster SRAM,” SRAM is used without expansion or a plain-language role. The surrounding explanation depends on the GPU memory hierarchy: the mechanism is that large per-token state is kept in fast on-chip/local memory rather than written to slower GPU main memory. Define SRAM at first use (for example, “fast on-chip scratch memory”) so a newcomer can follow why fusion reduces data traffic; preserve the distinction from HBM rather than implying that the state is never materialized at all.
